purpose: Review the 2021 Ihawan Spring Community Watershed survey as a Caraga inland-water source, preserving its historical scope and source labels while separating field reports from current presence, diet, safety, legal and app-ready claims.

studySource.title: Physico-chemical Properties and Fish Composition of Ihawan Spring Community Watershed, Tandag, Surigao del Sur, Philippines
studySource.studyArea: Ihawan Spring Community Watershed, Awasian, Tandag City, Surigao del Sur, Caraga, Philippines.
studySource.surveyPeriod: Seven sampling days in August 2018, as reported by the article.

accessAndReuse.visualReview: The complete publisher-hosted PDF text, including Methods, Tables 1-2 and Conclusion, was reviewed through the document viewer. Figure 1 was not visually inspected; no map geometry was read or digitized.
accessAndReuse.licenseAssessment: The reviewed article PDF does not state an article-specific Creative Commons license or grant Bangwit reuse permission. The journal landing page could not be retrieved during this review, so no journal-wide policy is inferred.
accessAndReuse.decision: Retain only bibliographic metadata and an attributed evidence-quality summary. Do not copy the article table, figure or photograph, nor publish source-derived species records or diet text in Bangwit without an item-specific rights review.

methods.design: Historical fish-composition and selected in-situ physicochemical assessment along an upstream-to-downstream watershed gradient.
methods.samplingEffort: The article reports a 1-km daytime sampling run lasting about 1.5 hours at each station and seven sampling days during August 2018. It does not clearly allocate the seven days among stations or provide visit-by-gear effort.
methods.reportedTotal: The conclusion reports 793 individuals, 23 species, 22 genera and 21 families. Table 2 gives relative-abundance percentages by station and species-richness values of 3, 9 and 23 for Stations 1-3; raw individual counts and a reproducible denominator are not supplied in the reviewed text.
methods.identificationAndVoucherStatus: The article says identification used field guides, published Philippine fish literature, FishBase and ichthyofauna-expert verification, and that morphometrics and on-site photographs were recorded. No voucher accession, repository or specimen-to-station photo crosswalk was located. The article says rare/endangered fish were returned after identification, photography and measurement.
methods.coordinateAssessment: The article provides a watershed locator and station coordinate strings with malformed seconds fields. They are not suitable for conversion into coordinates or geometry; no point or boundary is derived.

sourceTable.tableHeading: Checklist of collected fish species with percentage relative abundance per station and overall relative abundance per station in Ihawan Spring Community Watershed, Awasian, Tandag City, Surigao del Sur (August 2018).
sourceTable.printedNameNote: Names are retained as printed in the extracted article text, including Liza vaigeinsis; the Figure 2 caption renders a variant spelling. No taxonomic normalization or specimen re-identification is performed here.
sourceTable.feedingHabitColumn: Table 2 includes generalized feeding-habit phrases, but the reviewed methods do not describe gut-content, prey-identification or diet-sampling procedures or show the provenance of those phrases. They are not accepted as local natural-diet measurements or bait guidance.
sourceTable.statusLabels: The table prints abbreviated IUCN status labels and the article separately describes native, endemic, introduced and invasive categories. The assessments, reference dates and per-record basis were not independently verified; none are carried into app records.

reportedMeasurementsAndConflicts.fishComposition: The abstract reports Shannon-Wiener H=1.88 and Simpson's Dominance D=0.42; the Results report H=1.89 and D=1.24. The article does not reconcile the differences or clarify the index variant; these values are not reused.
reportedMeasurementsAndConflicts.waterQuality: Table 1 reports temperature (28.09, 29.05 and 29.48 °C), pH (7.8, 7.5 and 6.80) and dissolved oxygen (12, 10 and 8 mg/L) for three stations. Its pH remark says 'Above standards' despite listing a 6.5-8.5 interval. The narrative instead identifies 6.8 upstream and 7.9 downstream. The article mentions measuring CO2 in Methods but provides no corresponding result in Table 1.
reportedMeasurementsAndConflicts.salinityAndHabitat: No salinity measurement is reported. The source calls this a freshwater watershed, but Table 2 includes taxa associated in the paper with varied aquatic habitats, including Diodon holocanthus; the authors also speculate that rainy-season fish may move downstream to coastal waters. Station-level habitat and seasonal connectivity are not resolved by this single August survey.
reportedMeasurementsAndConflicts.permission: The acknowledgement says Tandag City Water District provided technical assistance and permission. This is not evidence of current fishing rules or a general public access right.

evidenceDecision.localityEvidence: A historical 2018 fish-collection report at three named reaches of the Ihawan Spring Community Watershed. It does not establish current occupancy, a complete watershed checklist or fine-scale mapped locations.
evidenceDecision.taxonEvidence: Twenty-three source binomials are transcribed as research candidates only. A separate Catalog of Fishes/WoRMS name-status screen is recorded in national-caraga-ihawan-spring-fish-taxonomy-crosscheck-20261031.json; name status is not specimen identity, and no voucher was independently reidentified.
evidenceDecision.dietEvidence: No diet or prey-composition data are accepted. The table's feeding-habit column is not a documented gut-content analysis and is not bait advice.
evidenceDecision.waterQualityEvidence: Historical readings from August 2018 with internal reporting inconsistencies and a narrow set of parameters. They are not current water-quality or potable-water evidence.
evidenceDecision.legalOrCatchabilityEvidence: None. Acknowledged study permission and statements about local practices do not establish current public fishing access, legal seasons, gear rules or catchability.
evidenceDecision.geometryEvidence: None. Malformed station coordinates and an unreviewed map figure do not support a point, polygon or navigation layer.
evidenceDecision.rights: Article-specific license and Bangwit publication permission were not verified.

limitations: One seven-day survey from August 2018 is not a current or complete fish inventory for Tandag, Surigao del Sur, Caraga or the Philippines.
No voucher accession, specimen repository or station-level identification crosswalk was located; name-status screening does not verify specimens.
The article has inconsistent diversity-index and pH interpretations; source measurements are not treated as current safety information.
The station coordinate strings are malformed and cannot support geometry; Figure 1 was not visually reviewed.
No salinity or seasonal comparison is provided, and the paper itself discusses possible downstream movement toward coastal waters.
The generalized feeding-habit phrases lack documented prey-sampling methods in this paper and do not establish local natural diet or bait advice.
The paper's IUCN, native/endemic/introduced/invasive labels and item-specific reuse rights remain unverified.
nextAction: Seek vouchers, station-level photographs or author clarification for Bostrychus expatria, Diodon holocanthus, Archamia bleekeri and Suezichthys gracilis; otherwise preserve all 23 labels as historical research-only evidence and continue the Caraga freshwater source queue.

references.supports: Publisher-hosted primary article text: study area, August 2018 sampling, methods, source labels, historical water measurements, reported counts, internal numerical conflicts and acknowledged study permission.
FAO AGRIS bibliographic record and abstract metadata only; not independent validation of the paper's field records.
